A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DTR research, with matching core methods and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack-success, benign-task performance, runtime, sensitivity, and token-reweighting experiments in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds model evaluations, VLGuard results, reference-transfer studies, stronger adaptive attacks, and a uniform-reweighting comparison.

M1.justification: The refusal-direction estimator, reversal safety-relevant shift, regularized token-weight optimization, clipping, early stopping, and token eviction remain unchanged, as does Algorithm 1. Specifying the regularizer's L2 norm in v3 Equation 8 clarifies the previously unspecified norm; it does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds VLGuard evaluation with unsafe-image/harmful-text and safe-image/harmful-text subsets. It also uses six additional reference corpora: Dolly-15K, GPT4All, Open-Orca/FLAN, StrongREJECT, JBB-Behaviors, and HarmBench. These substantially broaden the evaluated data sources and attack coverage while retaining the original benchmarks.

E2.justification: AdaShield, JailGuard, CoCA, and ShiftDC retain their original comparison membership. Appendix B.8 newly compares DTR against uniform visual-token scaling at four fixed values, but this additional comparator is evaluated through a single benign-image case study.

E3.justification: v3 adds Llama-4-Scout-17B evaluation, VLGuard subsets of 1,023 and 977 queries, and controlled reference-mixture and cross-category protocols. Appendix B.7 introduces RSS-minimizing PGD with an L-infinity budget of 16/255 on the first 50 HADES samples, using GPT-5.2 and a harmfulness score. These are substantial additional protocols; Appendix A's original defaults and benchmark selections remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test layer selection, learning-rate sensitivity, reference-source robustness, cross-category transfer, stronger defense-aware attacks, and uniform versus dynamic reweighting (Appendices B.2-B.5 and B.7-B.8). The original reference-count, optimization-step, lambda, eviction, and token-nulling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 3.2 newly reports multiple independent trials of random reference sampling and describes their variance as minimal. It supplies no trial count, seeds, or numerical uncertainty, so this is additional reporting rather than evidence of an increased run count. Figure 3's shaded variability bands already appear in v1.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained, including the relocated MME and lambda tables. Substantial new results include Llama-4-Scout HADES S+T+A ASR of 11.2% without DTR versus 8.4% with DTR, and adaptive-attack ASR of 68% versus 18% in the new 50-query setting. VLGuard, sensitivity, reference-transfer, and uniform-scaling results are also added; these are new evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and optimization formulation remain substantively equivalent. Splitting the mean-activation equation, renumbering equations, and explicitly identifying the L2 norm do not introduce new mathematical reasoning. The universality discussion cites other work and adds empirical interpretation, without a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding contribution statement retain the same central claims: DTR uses KV-cache optimization to defend against multimodal jailbreaks while preserving utility and efficiency, with a claimed first application of this approach to multimodal safety. The added evidence does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v3 develops substantial new interpretations about refusal directions being intrinsic and universal, visual reweighting protecting against textual attacks, robustness to RSS-targeting adversaries, and the necessity of dynamic rather than uniform scaling. The conclusion removes v1's reference-data limitation and adds combining DTR with decoding defenses as future work. Some new interpretations exceed their evidence, including the VLGuard metric confusion and inconsistent accuracy judgments in Table 14.

D1.justification: The replication link changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository, and v3 explicitly identifies the regularization norm. New experiments document reference-mixture counts, the adaptive perturbation budget, sample selection, and judge model. Core implementation disclosures, including AdamW, learning rate, iteration count, and H100 hardware, remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for the new model and reference datasets, plus COSMIC and cross-language refusal-direction research to support its universality discussion. The existing related-work organization and positioning of DTR relative to jailbreak defenses and KV-cache optimization remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The title changes, citations become numeric, and v3 adds subsection headings and acknowledgements, condenses some explanatory passages, and revises the conclusion. The appendix gains interleaved subsections, but the original narrative order and most existing prose remain recognizable; much of the expansion is new scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 changes the main document from single-column to two-column layout, extensively resizing and repositioning displays. Figure 5 changes from a two-by-two arrangement to one row, and eight tables plus a uniform-reweighting figure are added. The retained MME table also corrects category and total placement without changing its numerical values.

improvement.justification: The reference-transfer, sensitivity, and explicit adaptive-attack experiments address gaps in v1 and strengthen support for the unchanged method. The gains are limited by the small adaptive evaluation and reporting inconsistencies: Section 5.2 calls Table 9's 66.5%-to-7.4% refusal-heuristic change a harmfulness reduction, although harmfulness changes from 4.7% to 3.1%. Table 14 also labels a fire-extinguisher detail as a hallucination for uniform scaling but accurate for DTR. These weaknesses temper the otherwise useful expansion of evidence.
